answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a slashable stake bond and build a non-transferable record of verified work before it can take jobs. The bond makes mass identity creation expensive, because every fake agent must lock funds that are forfeited on fraud, while the work record cannot be copied from one identity to another. A newcomer starts with a tiny limit that grows only as the delta between completed jobs and disputes stays clean over time, like timber seasoning before it bears load, and a plume of new accounts from one operator stands out for review.
